title: Nick's in Greenwich Village and the Famous Door with Prima
summary: He starts at Nick's, stays ten years, then forms the Famous Door group with Louis Prima and splits with him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, uh, the band was pretty good. We were supposed to make a picture and, uh, for Damsel in distress, distressed with, uh, Ginger Rogers and Fetist there. So a little argument came up between Sharky and I, and I told Sharky to go. I didn't want to go. So then we, we stayed there, gradually against each other. And, uh, Nick made enough money there to build a new place across the street, which was 1937, December 10th. I'll never forget it because Red McKenzie was almost killed with a cab. We were carrying the tables across, you know, in the morning. We were drinking all the beer and helping them move. So I stayed at Nick's for 10 years. I was a house man down there. Every band came in there. Once I was a leader and I'd play with another band and I'd become a leader again. Bobby worked for me. I worked for Bobby. Pee-wee worked for me. I worked for Pee-wee. Same person. I would just switch it around. And we did terrific business. So then I leave there and I go with Miss Mills Calvacate, a girl and boy band. And Mills was booking me. Uh, in the meantime, I had met a man that's becoming very popular now. Miss Keely Smith's husband, uh, Louis Prima. Uh, he came up. When I was going good at Nick's, uh, he came up in New Orleans. He made a batch of records. He didn't know anybody. So he'd wake me up at nine o'clock in the morning and, uh, get me to go around to the agent's office. And I said, the agents knew me, but they knew in the back, but they didn't want to talk to Prima. They heard Prima played like Louis Armstrong. And I said, if they wanted the original, they'd get the Armstrong. Why get an imitator? So then I get an idea, a job for, through, uh, Cole and Lenny Hayton. I think there was three musicians on the Famous Door. So they'd come to me and ask me to get a band. They wanted a suitcase and whisper room with a wow-wow trombone. They wanted crazy effects, the sounds. So I said, well, I got just a guy for you, Louis Prima. So we had Prima and a piano player from New Orleans and, uh, Adams, Mike Adams was killed on the guitar. And this Ryan used to be with Jimmy Dorsey on bass. So we'd go and then we'd pack the joint. So I used to play a lot of bass notes and this arranger used to come in there. He was a big man, Gordon Jenkins. And he'd sit alongside of me and I'd play them low notes. He says, uh, hey, Bub, he says, can those things be arranged? I says, I don't know. You're an arranger. You should know that. I says, I'm just playing them. It's up to you to get them on the paper some kind of way. So Prima and I got into a little swivel and, uh, I went to Cole and I says, look, there's no use to working with this guy. I says, uh, I'm detracting from the guy and he don't like it. So Prima goes up and he says, I don't want to work with Broomers. He's detracting from me. I says, you're just two minutes too late, boy. I'll just quit you. I says, this was my job. Remember that. I gave it to you. This was supposed to be Brunus and his sextet. So then we caught it.
